labels.analyzeGlobalDesc: Checks collection structure and indexes integrity for all collections.
labels.vacuumGlobalDesc: Defragments and compacts collection storage to reclaim disk space.
labels.statementLanguage: the JSON command object this editor executes, one of {"collection": "<name>", "operation": "find", "filter": {...}, "options": {"projection": {...}, "sort": {...}, "skip": N, "limit": N}}, {"collection": "<name>", "operation": "findOne", "filter": {...}, "options": {"projection": {...}}}, {"collection": "<name>", "operation": "aggregate", "pipeline": [...]} (an aggregate takes no "filter" and no "options": write them as $match, $sort, $skip, $limit and $project stages), {"collection": "<name>", "operation": "count", "filter": {...}} and {"collection": "<name>", "operation": "distinct", "field": "<name>", "filter": {...}}, each with an optional "database": "<name>" (in the editor another database than the connected one; an agent run reads only the database its connection is bound to). A date is written {"$date": "2026-03-01T00:00:00Z"} and an ObjectId {"$oid": "<24 hex digits>"}, in a filter and in a pipeline alike: a plain string never equals a date or an ObjectId, so a filter that compares one with a string matches nothing. It is NOT mongosh shell syntax: a statement that starts with `db.`, or writes ISODate(...) or ObjectId(...), cannot be run here
labels.slowQueriesEmptyState: Query stats come from the database profiler - run db.setProfilingLevel() to start recording into system.profile.
